title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
statement: An array sorted in ascending order is rotated at an unknown pivot. Given the rotated array and an integer target, return the index of target, or -1 if it is not present. You must design an algorithm that runs in O(log n) time.
constraints: All values in nums are unique

examples.explanation: The array was rotated at index 4, and the value 0 sits exactly at the pivot.
The value 3 is not present in the array.

hints.content: The array is not fully sorted, so what property must still hold for half of the space to be discarded safely?
A rotation splits the array into two sorted halves. At least one half is still sorted.
Check whether the left half is sorted. If it is, the target is either inside it or to its right. Otherwise the right half is sorted.

low = 0, high = n - 1
while low <= high:
    mid = (low + high) / 2
    if nums[mid] == target: return mid
    if nums[low] <= nums[mid]:          // left half sorted
        if nums[low] <= target < nums[mid]: high = mid - 1
        else: low = mid + 1
    else:                                // right half sorted
        if nums[mid] < target <= nums[high]: low = mid + 1
        else: high = mid - 1
return -1
Testing sortedness with nums[low] <= nums[mid] instead of low < mid also handles the two element case.

pseudocode: if target is inside the left half: high = mid - 1
if target is inside the right half: low = mid + 1
invariant: If the target exists it is always inside the current range [low, high], which halves every iteration.
whyThisPattern: Rotation breaks the global order but not the local order. At every index at least one side of the midpoint is still sorted, so the comparison can always prove which half to discard. That is binary search with one extra observation per step.
bruteForce: A linear scan is O(n). At n = 100,000 that is 100,000 comparisons for every query, which is unacceptable when the problem explicitly requires O(log n): about 17 comparisons.
interviewExplanation: I keep a search range and take the midpoint each step. Because the array is a rotation, one of the two halves around the midpoint is always sorted, so I test which one it is and then check whether the target lies inside that sorted half, otherwise I move the bound the other way. Each iteration halves the range, giving O(log n) time and O(1) space.
commonMistakes: Assuming the whole array is sorted and using the plain template.
Using low < mid instead of nums[low] <= nums[mid] to detect sortedness, which breaks on two element ranges.
Overwriting mid or the bounds before the equality check.

animationSteps.title: The break point
animationSteps.description: Rotation creates exactly one place where order fails.
animationSteps.text: The array 4,5,6,7,0,1,2 is sorted except for the jump from 7 down to 0.

animationSteps.title: Search space
animationSteps.description: low = 0, high = 6, mid = 3 with value 7, target 3.
animationSteps.text: The search range runs from index 0 to 6. The midpoint index 3 holds the value 7, which is not the target 3.

animationSteps.title: Predict the move
animationSteps.description: Which side of the midpoint is still sorted?
animationSteps.text: The midpoint value is 7. Choose which side of the midpoint is still sorted.

payload.prompt: nums[mid] = 7, nums[low] = 4, nums[high] = 2. Which half is sorted?
payload.explanation: nums[low] = 4 is not greater than nums[mid] = 7, so the left half is sorted and the rotation is on the right.

animationSteps.title: Discard the left half
animationSteps.description: The target 3 is smaller than every value in [4, 7), so low moves to 4.
animationSteps.text: The target 3 is not inside the sorted range from 4 to 7, so the search space becomes index 4 to 6.

animationSteps.title: Second halving
animationSteps.description: mid = 5 holds 1, the left half is sorted, and 3 is not in [0, 1).
animationSteps.text: Midpoint index 5 holds the value 1 and the left half is sorted from 0 to 1. The target 3 is not inside it, so low moves to 6.

animationSteps.title: Last element checked
animationSteps.description: mid = 6 holds 2, which is not the target 3.
animationSteps.text: The last candidate is the value 2 at index 6. It is not the target 3, and the single element left in the range cannot contain it, so low moves past high.

animationSteps.title: Answer is -1
animationSteps.description: The search space is empty after three halvings.
animationSteps.text: Seven candidates were reduced to three halvings and then an empty range, so the target 3 is not present and the answer is -1.

payload.message: Answer -1 after three binary search steps.

options: A sorted array and a target value
An ascending array rotated at an unknown pivot, values unique, plus a target
An unsorted array and a target value
breakdown.explanation: A rotated ascending array of distinct values, plus the target. It is a binary search problem with one extra piece of damage, not a general search problem.

options: The index of the target, or -1
The index of the rotation pivot
breakdown.explanation: A position, or -1 when absent. Returning the value instead would be undefined on exactly the case that matters most.

breakdown.prompt: What has to be true at every step to keep this O(log n)?
options: At least one half of the remaining range is sorted
The midpoint always holds the target
The array must be rotated at the midpoint
breakdown.explanation: Halving every step is the requirement. What survives the rotation is that one half of the range is always sorted, so you can tell from the midpoint which half holds the target and discard the other.
